metadata.name: NIST AI RMF + ISO 42001 Knowledge Base
metadata.description: Core requirements for AI governance gap analysis

GOVERN.name: Govern
GOVERN.description: Cultivates and implements a culture of risk management. Cross-cutting function informing all others.

subcategories.description: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.
The characteristics of trustworthy AI are integrated into organizational policies, processes, procedures, and practices.
Processes, procedures, and practices are in place to determine the needed level of risk management activities based on the organization's risk tolerance.
The risk management process and its outcomes are established through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities.
Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes are planned and organizational roles and responsibilities clearly defined.
Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities.
Processes and procedures are in place for decommissioning and phasing out AI systems safely and in a manner that does not increase risks or decrease the organization's trustworthiness.
Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are documented and clear.
The organization's personnel and partners receive AI risk management training to enable them to perform their duties and responsibilities.
Executive leadership of the organization takes responsibility for decisions about risks associated with AI system development and deployment.

categories.name: Workforce diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility

subcategories.description: Decision-making related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks is informed by a diverse team (demographics, disciplines, experience, expertise, and backgrounds).
Policies and procedures are in place to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems.
Organizational policies and practices are in place to foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset in the design, development, deployment, and uses of AI systems.
Organizational teams document the risks and potential impacts of the AI technology they design, develop, deploy, evaluate, and use.
Organizational practices are in place to enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing.
Organizational policies and practices are in place to collect, consider, prioritize, and integrate feedback from those external to the team regarding potential individual and societal impacts.
Mechanisms are established to enable the team to regularly incorporate adjudicated feedback from relevant AI actors into system design and implementation.
Policies and procedures are in place that address AI risks associated with third-party entities, including risks of infringement of intellectual property or other rights.
Contingency processes are in place to handle failures or incidents in third-party data or AI systems deemed to be high-risk.

MAP.name: Map
MAP.description: Establishes the context to frame risks related to an AI system.

subcategories.description: Intended purposes, beneficial uses, laws, norms, expectations, and deployment settings are understood and documented.
Interdisciplinary AI actors, competencies, skills, and capacities for establishing context reflect demographic diversity and domain expertise.
The organization's mission and relevant goals for AI technology are understood and documented.
The business value or context of business use has been clearly defined or re-evaluated.
Organizational risk tolerances are determined and documented.
System requirements are elicited from and understood by relevant AI actors. Design decisions take socio-technical implications into account.
The specific tasks and methods used to implement the tasks that the AI system will support are defined.
Information about the AI system's knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans is documented.
Scientific integrity and TEVV considerations are identified and documented.
Potential benefits of intended AI system functionality and performance are examined and documented.
Potential costs, including non-monetary costs, which result from expected or realized AI errors or system functionality are examined and documented.
Targeted application scope is specified and documented based on the system's capability, established context, and AI system categorization.
Processes for operator and practitioner proficiency with AI system performance are defined, assessed, and documented.
Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies.
Approaches for mapping AI technology and legal risks of its components are in place, followed, and documented.
Internal risk controls for components of the AI system, including third-party AI technologies, are identified and documented.
Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact based on expected use, past uses, public incident reports, and feedback are identified and documented.
Practices and personnel for supporting regular engagement with relevant AI actors and integrating feedback are in place and documented.

A.2.name: Policies related to AI
A.2.description: To provide management direction and support for AI systems according to business requirements.

controls.name: AI policy
controls.description: The organization shall document a policy for the development or use of AI systems.

controls.name: Alignment with other organizational policies
controls.description: The organization shall determine where other policies can be affected by or apply to, the organization's objectives with respect to AI systems.

controls.name: Review of the AI policy
controls.description: The AI policy shall be reviewed at planned intervals or additionally as needed to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.

A.3.name: Internal organization
A.3.description: To establish accountability within the organization for the implementation, operation and management of AI systems.

controls.name: AI roles and responsibilities
controls.description: Roles and responsibilities for AI shall be defined and allocated according to the needs of the organization.

controls.name: Reporting of concerns
controls.description: The organization shall define and put in place a process to report concerns about the organization's role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle.

A.4.name: Resources for AI systems
A.4.description: To ensure that the organization accounts for the resources of the AI system to fully understand and address risks and impacts.

controls.name: Resource documentation
controls.description: The organization shall identify and document relevant resources required for the activities at given AI system life cycle stages.

controls.name: Data resources
controls.description: As part of resource identification, the organization shall document information about the data resources utilized for the AI system.

controls.name: Tooling resources
controls.description: As part of resource identification, the organization shall document information about the tooling resources utilized for the AI system.

controls.name: System and computing resources
controls.description: As part of resource identification, the organization shall document information about the system and computing resources utilized for the AI system.

controls.name: Human resources
controls.description: As part of resource identification, the organization shall document information about human resources and their competences utilized for the AI system.

A.6.name: AI system life cycle
A.6.description: To define the criteria and requirements for each stage of the AI system life cycle.

controls.name: Objectives for responsible development
controls.description: The organization shall identify and document objectives to guide the responsible development of AI systems, and integrate measures to achieve them.

controls.name: Processes for responsible design and development
controls.description: The organization shall define and document the specific processes for the responsible design and development of the AI system.

controls.name: AI system requirements and specification
controls.description: The organization shall specify and document requirements for new AI systems or material enhancements to existing systems.

controls.name: AI system verification and validation
controls.description: The organization shall define and document verification and validation measures for the AI system and specify criteria for their use.

controls.name: AI system deployment
controls.description: The organization shall document a deployment plan and ensure that appropriate requirements are met prior to deployment.

controls.name: AI system operation and monitoring
controls.description: The organization shall define and document the necessary elements for the ongoing operation of the AI system, including system and performance monitoring, repairs, updates and support.

controls.name: AI system technical documentation
controls.description: The organization shall determine what AI system technical documentation is needed for each relevant category of interested parties.

A.9.name: Use of AI systems
A.9.description: To ensure that the organization uses AI systems responsibly and per organizational policies.

controls.name: Processes for responsible use of AI systems
controls.description: The organization shall define and document the processes for the responsible use of AI systems.

controls.name: Objectives for responsible use of AI system
controls.description: The organization shall identify and document objectives to guide the responsible use of AI systems.

controls.name: Intended use of the AI system
controls.description: The organization shall ensure that the AI system is used according to the intended uses and its accompanying documentation.

A.10.name: Third-party and customer relationships
A.10.description: To ensure that the organization understands its responsibilities and remains accountable when third parties are involved.

controls.name: Allocating responsibilities
controls.description: The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.

controls.name: Suppliers
controls.description: The organization shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with its approach to responsible development and use.

controls.name: Customers
controls.description: The organization shall ensure that its responsible approach to the development and use of AI systems considers their customer expectations and needs.
